gloss: highest price; record high; peak value

definitions.gloss: highest price; record high; peak value
definitions.explanation: The highest price or value that something has reached, especially in financial markets. Used for stock prices, currency exchange rates, commodity prices, and other measurable values.

examples.japanese: {株価|かぶか}が{最高値|さいこうね}を{更新|こうしん}した。
examples.english: The stock price hit a new record high.

examples.japanese: {過去|かこ}{十年|じゅうねん}の{最高値|さいこうね}を{記録|きろく}した。
examples.english: It recorded the highest price in the past ten years.

examples.japanese: {金|きん}の{価格|かかく}が{史上|しじょう}{最高値|さいこうね}を{付|つ}け、{投資家|とうしか}の{間|あいだ}で{注目|ちゅうもく}を{集|あつ}めている。
examples.english: Gold prices have reached an all-time high, attracting attention among investors.

notes:
Composed of {最高|さいこう} (highest, maximum) and {値|ね} (price, value). A financial and economic term for peak prices.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {最高値|さいこうね}を{更新|こうしん}する: to set a new record high
- {最高値|さいこうね}を{記録|きろく}する: to record the highest price
- {最高値|さいこうね}を{付|つ}ける: to reach the highest price
- {史上|しじょう}{最高値|さいこうね}: all-time high
- {年初来|ねんしょらい}{最高値|さいこうね}: year-to-date high

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {最安値|さいやすね}: lowest price / record low — the opposite
- {高値|たかね}: high price — a high price, but not necessarily the highest ever
- {最高額|さいこうがく}: highest amount — similar but used for amounts of money rather than market prices

USAGE:
Read as さいこうね (not さいこうち). The reading {値|ね} is used for market prices, while {値|ち} (as in {最高値|さいこうち}) would mean "highest numerical value" in a more general mathematical sense.
